issue: Production database unreachable, entire service down after a routine maintenance task
root_cause: An engineer intended to clear a lagging secondary/replica database to fix replication drift, but ran the deletion command against the primary database by mistake. Backups had also been silently failing for weeks, so recovery required restoring from a stale staging snapshot.
solution: Restored from the most recent usable snapshot (several hours old, so some data was permanently lost). Long-term fixes included requiring a second engineer to verify any destructive database command before execution, active backup-success monitoring instead of silent failures, and regular restore drills.

issue: Global CDN and proxy outage after an internal permissions change
root_cause: A permissions update on an internal analytics database changed how a query returned table metadata, causing it to unexpectedly return duplicate rows. This bloated a configuration file used by the bot-detection system beyond a hard-coded size limit, which crashed the proxy software that handles most customer traffic.
solution: Rolled back to a last-known-good version of the configuration file to restore traffic, then fixed the query and added stricter validation and size limits on generated configuration files before they are distributed network-wide.

issue: Widespread cloud service disruption, new connections to a core database service failing region-wide
root_cause: A latent race condition in the automated DNS-management system for a managed database service caused two internal automation components to overwrite each other's DNS update, ultimately leaving an empty DNS record for the service's regional endpoint. Because so many other services depended on this database for internal coordination, the DNS failure cascaded into compute provisioning and other control-plane systems.
solution: Engineers manually restored the correct DNS records and disabled the automation that caused the conflict while it was fixed. Downstream systems that had accumulated bad state (like stale leases) needed additional manual recovery time even after the DNS issue itself was resolved.

issue: Server memory usage climbs steadily under load and the process eventually crashes, but heap dumps show no obvious leaked objects
root_cause: Memory was being lost to fragmentation rather than a true object leak: a low-level allocation call requesting aligned buffers was interacting badly with the system memory allocator, permanently fragmenting the memory pool over time even though every individual allocation was properly freed.
solution: Replaced the aligned-allocation pattern with a custom allocator that avoided the fragmentation-prone code path, which stopped the steady memory growth under sustained load.

issue: Background jobs stuck in a non-running state after a deployment, distribution service not picking up new work
root_cause: A deployment changed the data type of a database field used by the job-distribution service. Rows written before and after the deploy now had inconsistent types, and the distributor's strict schema validation rejected every row it scanned, so it silently stopped assigning work.
solution: A rollback did not fix the issue because it made even more rows unreadable; recovery required a hand-built deploy that ignored the affected field, followed by manual scaling to clear the backlog.

issue: DNS lookups failing intermittently for a subset of customers, some services returning name-resolution errors
root_cause: A script bug caused only the authoritative nameserver process (not the caching nameserver) to restart after an IP address change, so cached lookups began timing out. The subsequent fix attempt rebuilt the zone file using an internal API that itself depended on working DNS, producing a corrupted zone that returned domain-not-found errors for many records.
solution: Manually rebuilt and republished a correct zone file and restarted the affected nameserver processes; added a rule preventing DNS-dependent tooling from being used to fix DNS outages.

issue: Container orchestration cluster-wide outage right after a routine infrastructure deployment
root_cause: A DNS configuration change deployed to the infrastructure that runs the container orchestration cluster contained a defect that was not caught in testing environments. Once live, every service in the cluster lost the ability to resolve internal DNS names, so services could no longer discover or reach each other.
solution: Rolled back the configuration change to restore DNS resolution, then improved pre-production testing to include the specific DNS resolution path that had gone untested.

issue: Site-wide read outage after a routine database configuration rollout
root_cause: A configuration change rolled out to production databases changed how hosts responded to routing-service health checks. The health-check system incorrectly marked the read-only endpoint as unhealthy, taking it out of rotation even though the databases themselves were fine.
solution: Reverted the configuration change to restore correct health-check responses; read traffic resumed within the hour once the endpoint was marked healthy again.

issue: Legitimate customer traffic being blocked by the web application firewall with no recent deploys to explain it
root_cause: A gap in access controls allowed a change to be made to a firewall configuration outside of the normal infrastructure-as-code pipeline. Because the change wasn't recorded in the deployment history, on-call responders spent significant time chasing unrelated leads (like recent code deploys and CORS errors) before automated drift detection revealed the untracked firewall change as the real cause.
solution: Reverted the out-of-band firewall change and tightened access controls so that infrastructure changes outside the standard pipeline are blocked or immediately flagged.

issue: EC2 instance launches and other AWS services degraded in one region, seemingly unrelated to any recent change in those services
root_cause: A dependent internal system (the server lease-management system) stores its state in the same database that suffered the DNS outage. When it could not reach that database, it began marking healthy physical servers as unavailable and aggressively retried lease renewals, creating a feedback loop of load that slowed recovery even after the original DNS problem was fixed.
solution: Engineers throttled and manually reset the lease-management system's retry behavior to break the feedback loop, allowing server capacity to gradually come back online.

issue: E-commerce site completely down during a traffic spike from a marketing campaign, despite spare server capacity being available
root_cause: A misconfiguration in the cluster resource manager prevented new service instances from being scheduled even though the underlying hardware had room for them, so the system couldn't scale out to absorb the traffic spike.
solution: Corrected the resource-manager configuration to allow scheduling onto the available hardware, and added load testing ahead of future marketing campaigns to catch similar scaling limits in advance.

issue: In-VPC DNS queries failing for EC2 instances in one AWS region
root_cause: A configuration change intended for a specific setting incorrectly removed the minimum-healthy-host threshold for the internal DNS resolver fleet, causing the system to fall back to a very low default. The resolver fleet's healthy host count then dropped below what was needed to serve queries reliably.
solution: Manually restored resolver capacity, then added semantic validation for this class of configuration change plus rate-limiting on how quickly hosts can be removed from the fleet.

issue: Global outage of a major social media platform and its associated apps, all internal tools also inaccessible
root_cause: A configuration change to the company's backbone routers was intended to assess available network capacity but instead disconnected the company's data centers from the internet entirely, including the very systems needed to remotely fix the problem.
solution: Engineers had to gain physical access to data center hardware to manually correct the router configuration, since the standard remote-access tools were themselves unreachable during the outage.

issue: Cluster nodes repeatedly restarting due to out-of-memory crashes, cluster leadership flapping between nodes
root_cause: Under sustained high load, memory usage on cluster nodes grew steadily until each node ran out of memory and crashed; the cluster would elect a new leader and continue, masking the underlying leak from the customer's perspective while engineers traced it to a memory allocation pattern specific to certain workload conditions.
solution: Identified and patched the specific allocation pattern causing unbounded growth, then added proactive memory-growth monitoring to catch the same pattern before it caused crashes in other clusters.

issue: Backend routing sending requests to the wrong service after a CDN configuration change
root_cause: A CDN configuration change set the backend target inside a request-handling function, but a later step in the same configuration restarted request processing, which reset the backend target back to the first option in the list rather than the intended load-balanced target.
solution: Corrected the configuration so the backend target survives the restart step, and added a test case that specifically checks backend routing after this kind of mid-request restart.

issue: Payment API requests slowing down and failing under normal traffic, no recent code deploy to explain it
root_cause: A routine database schema change to add an index was misinterpreted by internal tooling as two separate operations (a removal followed by an addition) instead of one modification. The brief window where the index didn't exist caused queries that depended on it to slow down dramatically, and the resulting load backed up the whole database.
solution: Restored the index and fixed the tooling so that modifying an existing index description is handled as a single atomic operation rather than being decomposed into a remove-then-add sequence.

issue: Payment API median response time jumps from ~120ms to multiple seconds, checkouts stalling for many customers at once
root_cause: A metadata write path used during payment creation saturated a database cluster after a traffic increase combined with a reduced number of available connections in the connection pool. As requests queued, client-side retries added further load to the same overloaded pool, amplifying the slowdown across thousands of integrated platforms.
solution: Reporting suggests recovery involved relieving the connection pool bottleneck and separating client retry traffic from core request queues to prevent the same amplification loop in future incidents.
note: Source is a third-party retrospective analysis rather than an official Stripe postmortem; verify specifics against an official source if available before relying on this for evaluation.

issue: API calls unexpectedly getting rate-limited far more often than usual after a routine maintenance window
root_cause: Maintenance on the API token-management system inadvertently changed how token validation interacted with the rate-limiting system, causing much stricter rate-limit enforcement to be applied broadly, including to calls that should have been exempt.
solution: Reverted the token-validation/rate-limiting interaction to the correct behavior; added monitoring so this kind of enforcement-rate spike is caught automatically instead of relying on customer reports.

issue: Users unable to log in or send messages platform-wide, error rates spiking after a scheduled infrastructure change
root_cause: A caching-layer rollout caused a cache-refill query to scan far more data than intended, driving up load on the primary datastore. The system's own automated response (throttling client connections) was first tuned too aggressively, then had to be corrected in smaller increments while engineers rewrote the underlying query to read only the missing data rather than scanning entire shards.
solution: Reduced load via a client connection/boot-rate throttle, corrected the throttle in careful increments to avoid overshooting, rewrote the inefficient query to read only missing cache entries, and allowed it to read from replicas since the underlying data could tolerate staleness.

issue: Site-wide availability drops sharply during a routine, weeks-long schema migration that had run without issue up to that point
root_cause: The final rename step of a large MySQL schema migration triggered a semaphore deadlock on a significant portion of read replicas. Deadlocked replicas entered crash-recovery, which pushed more load onto the remaining healthy replicas and cascaded into a broader availability drop.
solution: Recovered the deadlocked replicas and restored capacity; follow-up work focused on changing how the final migration step is executed so it no longer triggers this deadlock pattern on read replicas.

issue: Streaming write API returning elevated error rates for several hours with no obvious external trigger
root_cause: A sudden increase in incoming and logging traffic interacted with a bug in an internal streaming RPC library, triggering a deadlock that overloaded the write-API's streaming frontend.
solution: Mitigated the overload and addressed the RPC library bug that made the frontend susceptible to deadlocking under a traffic increase.

issue: Dashboard, mobile app, and API all briefly unavailable at the same time shortly after a database version upgrade
root_cause: After a Postgres major-version upgrade, an audit-logging extension that had passed staging tests was re-enabled in production. A routine table-creation migration triggered a pathological interaction with that extension, which hung while holding critical locks and ignored timeout signals, blocking other database operations across multiple products at once.
solution: Restarted the primary database to forcibly break the deadlock (a short hard outage), then removed the problematic extension entirely rather than attempting to reconfigure it.

issue: New authorizations and deployments failing platform-wide with a database-level error, unrelated to any application code change
root_cause: A foreign key column was defined with a smaller integer data type than the primary key column it referenced. When the primary key's values exceeded what the smaller foreign-key type could hold, inserts began failing with an overflow error, blocking creation of new authorizations and, downstream, new deployments.
solution: Corrected the mismatched column data type so the foreign key could represent the full range of primary key values, resolving the overflow and restoring the ability to create authorizations and deployments.

issue: New feature under heavy testing causes hangs and crashes in the test suite, but only intermittently and only with the new code path
root_cause: A months-long performance rewrite of core I/O handling introduced a native code path (needed because the new high-performance async I/O API wasn't available in managed code). The new code had a subtle interlocking bug that only manifested as a race condition under certain timing conditions, making it hang or crash unpredictably rather than failing consistently.
solution: Caught during testing rather than in production; resolved by isolating and fixing the specific interlock logic in the native code path, after extended debugging effort by multiple engineers.

issue: A .NET service consumes unexpectedly large amounts of memory under certain customer workloads, but only in one specific hosting environment
root_cause: A single large-buffer request caused heap fragmentation under a particular web server configuration; the fragmented memory wasn't reclaimed unless the system came under active memory pressure, so usage crept upward until the process needed a restart under that hosting environment specifically.
solution: Identified the environment-specific trigger by reproducing inside the actual hosting environment (rather than a local dev server) and adjusted memory handling to avoid the fragmentation-prone allocation pattern.

issue: Suspicious login activity flagged on a third-party support engineer's account, unclear how much customer data was exposed
root_cause: An attacker took remote control of a workstation belonging to a support engineer at an outsourced customer-support vendor for about 25 minutes. From that single workstation the attacker could view limited information in a couple of internal tools, but the vendor's use of shared/contracted devices meant the identity provider itself had no direct visibility into the compromise until the vendor's forensic report came back weeks later.
solution: Terminated the vendor relationship, began directly managing and monitoring any third-party device that accesses internal support tools, and restricted how much customer information a support engineer's view can expose going forward.

issue: Customer OAuth tokens, API keys, and SSH keys may have been exposed after the company's database provider was breached
root_cause: The third-party database provider hosting the company's MongoDB instance was itself breached, and that database held GitHub OAuth tokens, Heroku API tokens, AWS IAM keys, and SSH deploy/user keys belonging to customers.
solution: Shut down the site and all running builds immediately upon notification, then coordinated with GitHub, Heroku, and AWS to revoke every OAuth token, API token, IAM key, and SSH key that had been issued, and rotated all of the company's own keys and caches before resuming service.

issue: Cryptocurrency funds diverted from a smart-contract wallet almost immediately after a supposedly minor UI change was deployed
root_cause: A large code change was mislabeled internally as a routine UI update, so it received far less scrutiny during review than a change of that size and risk warranted. The change actually contained a security flaw in the wallet contract logic that let an attacker divert funds once it was live and in use by third parties.
solution: A portion of the funds was proactively redirected to a safe address by a white-hat rescue effort before attackers could reach it. Longer-term, the incident became a widely cited case for requiring risk-proportional code review labeling and stricter audit processes for financial smart contracts.

issue: Six-hour partial outage of the API and admin dashboard, edge network itself unaffected
root_cause: The control-plane databases (separate from the globally distributed edge network) relied on redundant switches within each rack, but a failing switch produced inconsistent state information to different database cluster members -- a Byzantine fault. This caused repeated, disruptive leader elections that left the cluster read-only for extended periods, since the election couldn't resolve while the faulty switch was intermittently reachable to some nodes and not others.
solution: Manually intervened to remove the faulty switch from service so a stable leader election could complete, then reviewed how cluster leader-election logic handles conflicting/partial information from a partially-failed component rather than assuming failures are all-or-nothing.

issue: Long outage of a data-center-hosted service; on-site staff unable to resolve it quickly on their own
root_cause: A control-plane and analytics system running across three physically separate data centers relied on a colocation provider's backup power arrangement. When utility power was interrupted, the backup generator arrangement didn't behave as expected, and it took considerable time to get clarity from the colocation provider on why, since key technical details about their power failover setup weren't fully documented or communicated in advance.
solution: Worked with the colocation provider to restore power and bring systems back online, then pushed to get full documentation of the provider's power failover design and clearer communication commitments for any future incident of this kind.

issue: Regional cloud compute service degraded, engineers unsure at first whether it's a network or hardware problem
root_cause: A hardware failure in networking equipment reduced available network capacity in the region below what was needed to serve traffic reliably, and automated failover did not fully compensate for the reduced capacity.
solution: Manually rerouted traffic and restored capacity by replacing/repairing the affected hardware; added additional capacity headroom so a single piece of failed equipment doesn't push the region below serviceable capacity.
note: Extracted from a brief public incident summary; recommend reading the full incident report at the source URL before finalizing wording for the paper.

issue: Small hosting provider goes fully offline, customers can't reach their sites or the admin console
root_cause: A hardware failure at the hosting provider's data center took down the underlying infrastructure that customer sites and the control panel both depended on, with no immediate automated failover in place for a failure of that specific component.
solution: Restored service once the failed hardware was replaced/repaired; the postmortem discussion afterward focused on adding redundancy for the specific component that had no failover.
note: Read the full post at the source URL for exact technical specifics before using this as an evaluation example.

issue: Old, forgotten server turns out to be an entry point for an attacker who accessed production systems
root_cause: A retired prototype machine had never been decommissioned and was still running software with a known critical vulnerability (Shellshock). That machine also still held secret keys, which the attacker used to pivot from the vulnerable prototype into production systems.
solution: Took the affected systems offline, rotated all exposed secrets, and instituted a decommissioning process to ensure old/unused machines are fully retired (including credential revocation) rather than left running indefinitely.

issue: Employee found to have quietly moved company cryptocurrency funds out over the course of a month before anyone noticed
root_cause: Weak internal security practices, including insufficiently restricted access to funds and a lack of monitoring/alerting on fund movements, allowed a single employee to conduct three separate unauthorized transfers over roughly a month without detection.
solution: According to public reporting, the company overhauled internal access controls and monitoring after the incident came to light, though the funds themselves were reportedly not recovered.

issue: Newly launched cloud region has an unexplained widespread network capacity problem
root_cause: A hardware/power related failure at the underlying infrastructure provider reduced available capacity below the level automated systems were designed to handle gracefully.
solution: Provider-level hardware issue was resolved by the infrastructure vendor; the cloud service provider added monitoring to detect this class of upstream capacity reduction earlier next time.
note: Brief public incident summary; verify exact wording against the source before including in a published dataset.

issue: Payment webhook deliveries silently stop arriving for a subset of merchants after a routine infrastructure change
root_cause: A change to message-queue infrastructure supporting webhook delivery caused a subset of delivery workers to lose their connection to the queue without raising an alert, so webhooks queued for those workers were never delivered until manually detected by affected merchants.
solution: Added active health checks on webhook delivery workers instead of relying on the absence of errors, and manually replayed the missed webhook deliveries once identified.
note: This entry paraphrases community/HN discussion of payment-infrastructure incidents rather than an official postmortem; treat as lower-confidence until corroborated by a primary source, or replace with a verified entry before final dataset use.

issue: API error rates climb steadily over several hours with no single obvious trigger, unlike a typical sudden outage
root_cause: Frontend traffic increased gradually while a backend database service was already running close to capacity; a database index design concentrated certain metadata on only a few shards, and a short cache expiration time forced frequent database refreshes, so read contention on those few shards grew disproportionately as traffic rose.
solution: According to the incident report, mitigations focused on redistributing the concentrated metadata across more shards and lengthening the cache expiration window to reduce refresh frequency and read contention.
note: This detail appeared inside a third-party aggregator page alongside an unrelated Slack incident; verify against Google's own incident report before relying on it for evaluation.

issue: Widespread messaging outage, engineers initially unsure if it's a database, cache, or networking problem
root_cause: Static routing configuration had not kept pace with recent infrastructure growth, so updated routing information from the database layer could not reach the web application layer. Clients ended up working from stale gateway data, causing rising error rates and degraded functionality across the platform.
solution: Restored correct routing information to the web layer and began treating routing configuration as something that must scale dynamically with infrastructure growth rather than being maintained as a static value.

issue: Site down after a maintenance window that was supposed to be routine and low-risk
root_cause: Sending multicast traffic without first ensuring the network switches were properly configured to handle it caused a global outage rather than the isolated, contained effect that had been expected.
solution: Reconfigured switches to handle multicast traffic correctly and added pre-maintenance checks specifically for multicast-related network configuration before future rollouts.

issue: Cloud storage backing multiple products (not just one) becomes slow and error-prone at the same time
root_cause: A configuration change meant to address rising demand for metadata storage instead overloaded part of the underlying blob-lookup system, and because several products share that same storage layer, the overload cascaded into visible problems across multiple, seemingly unrelated products at once.
solution: Rolled back the configuration change and throttled metadata storage demand until the blob-lookup system's load returned to normal, then added capacity headroom to that shared layer.
note: Brief public incident summary; read the full report at the source URL before finalizing wording.

issue: Two-hour-plus outage in one geographic region caused by a latent bug in networking code that had presumably been running fine for a long time
root_cause: A new infrastructure feature triggered a previously-dormant bug inside internal network load-balancer code, which had gone unnoticed until this specific new feature interacted with it in production.
solution: Rolled back the newly introduced feature to stop triggering the bug, then patched the underlying load-balancer code defect directly.
note: Brief public incident summary; verify against full report before final dataset inclusion.

issue: Load balancer returning 404 errors for valid requests, affecting several downstream cloud products at once
root_cause: A latent bug in a network configuration service was triggered during what should have been routine system operation, producing incorrect load-balancer behavior that surfaced as 404 errors for legitimate requests.
solution: Rolled back to known-good load-balancer configuration state and patched the underlying configuration-service bug that allowed the incorrect state to be generated in the first place.
note: Brief public incident summary; verify against full report before final dataset inclusion.

issue: Reduced throughput for batch and streaming workloads over roughly a day, real-time/user-facing traffic unaffected
root_cause: A combination of planned repair work and a routine network software upgrade rollout reduced available capacity for lower-priority traffic classes; the system correctly deprioritized batch/streaming work to protect user-facing traffic, but that meant sustained degradation for the deprioritized workloads until the underlying work finished.
solution: Completed the repair and upgrade work as planned; capacity for lower-priority traffic classes returned to normal once both were finished, with no separate remediation needed beyond completing the scheduled work.

issue: Web dynos fail to start after a routine remote configuration change, application deploys stuck
root_cause: An automated remote configuration change did not fully propagate to all the systems responsible for starting web dynos, leaving some of them working from stale configuration and unable to start new dynos correctly.
solution: Manually verified and re-propagated the configuration to all affected systems, and added a completion check to confirm remote configuration changes have actually reached every target system before considering the change complete.
note: Brief public incident summary; read the full report at the source URL before finalizing wording.

issue: 'git push heroku main' silently fails to deploy new code even though the push itself succeeds
root_cause: An incorrect deployment process meant that newly introduced configuration variables were not actually being used by the running application, so code that depended on those variables behaved as if they were never set, even though the push and build steps reported success.
solution: Corrected the deployment process so new configuration variables are properly picked up and used at runtime, and added a way to verify that a deploy is actually using the intended configuration rather than just checking build/push success.

issue: Storage service memory usage climbing steadily on a subset of servers over a weekend, no application errors logged
root_cause: A background reporting agent on storage servers couldn't reach its data-collection endpoint. Rather than degrading gracefully, it kept retrying in a way that slowly leaked memory, and monitoring didn't alert on the leak because storage servers already used memory dynamically in normal operation, masking the abnormal growth.
solution: By the time the leak was severe enough to disrupt request handling and failover attempts also failed, the servers had to be manually restarted; follow-up work added graceful-degradation handling and specific alerting for this reporting agent's memory usage.

issue: Personal access token with unusually broad scopes shows up being used for pushes it shouldn't be making
root_cause: A personal access token that had recently been given elevated scopes leaked out of a continuous-integration system, giving whoever obtained it push access to several of the organization's repositories.
solution: Revoked the leaked token immediately, audited what it had been used for, and reviewed why a CI system's token had broader scopes than necessary in the first place (least-privilege review).

issue: Malicious packages discovered in a widely-used package registry, apparently published by a trusted maintainer account
root_cause: An attacker compromised the package-registry account credentials of a legitimate project maintainer (not through a platform vulnerability, but likely credential theft or reuse) and used the compromised account to publish malicious packages that looked like they came from a trusted source.
solution: Removed the malicious packages, secured/reset the compromised maintainer account, and the incident became a widely cited case for enabling two-factor authentication on package-publishing accounts.

issue: Repository credentials found sitting in a source code repo, unclear how long they'd been exposed
root_cause: A hosted source-code repository contained credentials that granted access to production backups, including hashed passwords, with the exposure only discovered after the fact rather than caught during development.
solution: Rotated the exposed credentials immediately, restricted backup access, and added scanning to catch credentials committed into repositories before they can be exposed this way again.

issue: Cluster nodes crash almost simultaneously, at first suspected to be a coordinated attack rather than a bug
root_cause: A double-free memory bug was exposed by a routine database update; the bug required a specific timing delay to trigger, which existed in production but not in the staging environment, so it wasn't caught before rollout and caused near-simultaneous crashes across the fleet.
solution: Rolled back the update and fixed the double-free bug, then adjusted staging environments to include realistic timing delays so this class of timing-dependent bug is more likely to surface before reaching production.
note: This is a well-known but sparsely documented historical incident; verify specifics against a primary source before relying on it for evaluation.

issue: Phone network calls failing on a massive scale immediately after a routine, seemingly unrelated maintenance event
root_cause: A defect in switch software created a race condition; after a planned brief outage, resumption messages sent during recovery re-triggered the race, causing repeated switch reboots that propagated iteratively through the network as recovering switches sent more resumption messages, retriggering the same race elsewhere.
solution: Engineers eventually had to slow the resumption/recovery process across the network to stop it from repeatedly retriggering the race, allowing the network to stabilize; longer-term the underlying software defect was fixed.

issue: Storage operations across an entire cloud platform grind to a halt, seemingly unrelated services also can't complete basic operations
root_cause: A lock couldn't be obtained on shared metadata servers because two unrelated things collided: routine database maintenance that periodically needs to lock parts of the table, and a separate query that -- unnecessarily -- was requesting a much broader (global) lock than it actually needed for its task.
solution: Fixed the overly broad query to request only the specific lock scope it actually needed, removing the unnecessary contention with routine maintenance locking.

issue: Every customer instance in an entire datacenter reboots at once during what was supposed to be limited maintenance on a handful of machines
root_cause: An operator used a maintenance tool with lax input validation to reboot a small, specific set of servers, but forgot to include a flag restricting scope to just those servers -- so the command defaulted to rebooting every server in the datacenter instead.
solution: Once the scope of the mistake was clear, engineers worked through the resulting overload on boot-related infrastructure and manual recovery of affected systems; longer-term, the tool's input validation and default behavior (defaulting to "all" rather than requiring explicit, narrow scoping) were identified as needing to change.

issue: Login page and dashboard briefly show odd cross-account data before the site goes fully down for maintenance
root_cause: Queues used to hold requests and responses for an AI system's cache became corrupted and got out of sequence, which meant some responses were served to the wrong user, unintentionally revealing details like another user's activity history and some billing information.
solution: Took the affected system down while the sequencing bug in the cache/queue handling was fixed, and notified affected users about what categories of information may have been exposed to someone else.

issue: Database comes back online after a restart but every service using it starts throwing filesystem-related errors instead of running smoothly
root_cause: After the primary database locked up and had to be restarted, it came back up with the wrong underlying filesystem mounted, so the data it was serving from didn't match what was expected, causing a global outage rather than the smooth restart that was expected.
solution: Corrected which filesystem was mounted, restarted the database properly, and verified data integrity before fully restoring traffic.

issue: A well-known, heavily-used cloud storage service in one region goes fully down after what was supposed to be a small, well-understood maintenance task
root_cause: An engineer was debugging a minor issue using an established, previously-safe playbook; one of the commands intended to remove a small number of servers was entered with a typo, which caused a much larger set of servers -- including ones supporting critical parts of the storage system itself -- to be removed instead. Because those systems hadn't been fully restarted in a long time, the restart process itself took far longer than expected, extending the outage.
solution: Restarted the affected critical subsystems (a slower process than anticipated due to their long uptime), and added safeguards to the operational tooling to prevent single commands from being able to remove capacity beyond a safe threshold, regardless of what's typed.

issue: A cloud provider's core storage request-handling fleet becomes overloaded and slow, without any unusual traffic spike from customers
root_cause: Corrupted messages within the storage system caused an internal function tracking distributed server state to behave incorrectly, consuming far more resources than normal on the fleet that processes storage requests, degrading performance even though external customer traffic hadn't actually increased.
solution: Identified and corrected the message-corruption issue and the resulting resource-consuming behavior in the state-tracking function, restoring normal resource usage on the request-processing fleet.
note: Brief public summary; verify against the specific AWS message/postmortem before finalizing.

issue: A storage service's health-monitoring dashboard shows the wrong state for load balancers, and attempts to fix it seem to make things worse
root_cause: A maintenance process was accidentally run against the production load balancer's live state data instead of a test copy, corrupting or altering the state data that the load balancing service relied on to make routing decisions.
solution: Restored the load balancer state data from a known-good backup and added safeguards (like environment checks) to the maintenance tooling to prevent it from being run against production state data by accident again.

issue: Some HTTP responses from edge servers contain fragments of completely unrelated customers' private data -- cookies, auth tokens, even POST body content
root_cause: A parsing bug in edge-server software caused it to occasionally include leftover memory contents in outgoing HTTP responses; because that memory could contain sensitive data from previous, unrelated requests (cookies, authentication tokens, POST bodies), some responses leaked private information belonging to other customers or requests entirely.
solution: Disabled the affected parsing feature immediately upon discovery to stop further leakage, worked with search engines to purge cached copies of leaked data from their indexes, and patched the underlying parser bug before re-enabling the feature.

issue: A large government website launches on schedule but immediately becomes unusable for the vast majority of people trying to sign up
root_cause: According to widely reported post-incident analysis, the failure stemmed from broad organizational and process problems rather than a single technical bug: fragmented ownership across many contractors, insufficient end-to-end load testing before launch, and a lack of a single technical leader accountable for overall system integration and performance.
solution: A dedicated technical response team was brought in after launch to rebuild and stabilize the site over the following months, including consolidating technical decision-making and running realistic load tests that had been skipped before the original launch.
note: This is a well-known organizational/process failure rather than a single discrete technical incident; treat differently from other entries in evaluation since it may not fit a typical single-cause RCA pattern.

issue: A hardware-manufacturer's chips occasionally produce very slightly wrong answers on a specific class of math operation, discovered by an outside academic rather than internal testing
root_cause: A scripting bug caused certain entries to be omitted from a lookup table used by the chip's division logic, so a small set of specific division operations occasionally produced incorrect results; the bug wasn't caught internally because a mathematical proof of the divider's correctness rested on an incorrect assumption that all necessary table entries were present.
solution: Once identified, redesigned the affected chip revision to correct the divider logic and, after public pressure, offered replacements for affected chips even though the practical impact for most users was extremely rare.

issue: A trading firm's automated system starts sending huge volumes of erratic, unintended orders across dozens of stocks the moment markets open, with no human trader involved
root_cause: A new software release was deployed to eight production servers, but one of the eight still had an old feature flag left enabled from a previous, retired testing tool. That flag reactivated a long-dormant, unused code path (an old order-testing feature) which began generating a flood of unintended live orders as soon as the market opened, since nothing distinguished that one server's stale configuration from the other seven until the erroneous orders were already executing.
solution: The firm had to identify which of the eight servers was misconfigured and halt/disable it, but by the time trading was stopped, tens of thousands of erroneous trades had already executed across many stocks; the financial losses were severe enough that the firm required emergency external funding to remain solvent.
note: No official internal postmortem from Knight Capital is publicly available; this account is reconstructed from the SEC's public administrative proceeding and widely-cited secondary analysis. Verify specifics against the SEC filing before final use.

issue: A configuration error in BGP prefix advertising caused a major outage across 19 Cloudflare data centers, impacting traffic routing.
root_cause: An incorrect ordering of BGP advertised prefixes caused edge routers in 19 data centers to stop announcing IP space, dropping all incoming traffic.
solution: Corrected the BGP advertisement prefixes sequence and updated routing verification tooling.

issue: A bad router rule configuration deployed to edge network routers caused them to crash, taking down the entire CDN service globally.
root_cause: A deployment of a bad routing rule configuration triggered a bug in the edge routers, causing their CPU usage to spike to 100% and crashing the routing processes across the global network.
solution: Rolled back the bad routing rule configuration and implemented CPU limits and stricter checks for router rule updates.

issue: Global service discovery component became unavailable for several hours after a bad configuration in a single client caused a cascading failure.
root_cause: A bad configuration in a service discovery client triggered an infinite loop of connection retries when a dependent service went down, which overloaded and crashed the central service discovery server.
solution: Implemented client-side backoff and rate limiting on service discovery requests, and added circuit breakers to the central server.

issue: Enom registrar platform experienced widespread downtime and lookup delays for hours during a planned cloud migration.
root_cause: A complex database and network cutover to a new cloud infrastructure encountered sync and routing failures, causing replication delays and corrupting DNS records.
solution: Extended the maintenance window, resolved the database synchronization locks, and restored DNS records.

issue: The public API and dashboard became completely unavailable due to a database cluster outage.
root_cause: A bad configuration setting combined with a hardware failure on the primary database node prevented the secondary replica from auto-promoting, causing a split-brain condition.
solution: Manually forced the promotion of the secondary replica and corrected the cluster routing configuration.

issue: Several Google services, including Gmail and Google Calendar, suffered a widespread outage due to a configuration bug.
root_cause: An automated configuration deployment system generated a corrupt configuration file that set quota limits to zero, which disabled access to metadata databases.
solution: Rolled back the configuration change and updated the autogeneration validation checks to block zero-value quotas.

issue: A bad configuration update caused a global quota service to fail, leading to widespread failures across Gmail and other Google services.
root_cause: A bad configuration change in a quota service triggered a deadlock in its query engine, causing it to block all incoming quota check requests, which cascaded to downstream services.
solution: Restarted the quota service with the configuration reverted and added rate-limiting on client retry requests.

issue: Google Search flagged every website on the internet with a security warning stating that the site may harm the user's computer.
root_cause: An engineer accidentally checked in a single forward slash character ('/') into the blacklisted URL database, which matched all URLs since all URLs contain a slash.
solution: Removed the slash from the blacklist and updated check-in validation to prevent single-character URL matches.

issue: The production database was accidentally deleted, causing website downtime and loss of 7 hours of user data.
root_cause: An engineer accidentally ran a database deletion command against the production environment instead of staging. Backups were only taken once daily.
solution: Restored database from the most recent daily backup, resulting in a permanent loss of 7 hours of data. Added multi-factor confirmation for destructive database commands.

issue: Widespread Azure Storage outage affected multiple cloud services globally, preventing virtual machines from starting.
root_cause: A bad configuration change deployed to the storage front-end servers caused an infinite loop in the request parsing logic, exhausting the connection pool.
solution: Reverted the configuration change and restarted the front-end servers.

issue: A water treatment plant shut down and issued a do-not-consume order due to a fluoride overdose.
root_cause: An operator accidentally pressed the wrong button on a control panel, which bypassed safety limits and pumped excessive fluoride into the water supply.
solution: Shut down the plant, flushed the system, and updated the control panel to require physical keys or double-confirmation for chemical adjustments.

issue: Widespread financial transaction failures and data loss occurred following a database failover.
root_cause: An unexpected hardware failure triggered an RDS Multi-AZ failover. However, the target MySQL database was misconfigured with asynchronous replication settings that had not been updated, leading to data drift and loss.
solution: Manually synced transaction logs from secondary storage and corrected the MySQL replication configurations.

issue: DNS record resolution for static.crates.io failed for 15 minutes, blocking crate downloads globally.
root_cause: During a routine infrastructure deployment, both the TLS certificates and DNS records were re-created simultaneously, causing a propagation delay.
solution: Updated records in the DNS registrar and separated certificate renewal from DNS record updates.

issue: All crate downloads from crates.io failed for 13 minutes, causing millions of failed cargo build requests.
root_cause: A deployment introduced a bug in the download URL generation logic, causing it to return malformed URLs for all download requests.
solution: Rolled back the deployment and added unit tests covering download URL generation.

issue: Stack Overflow and the Stack Exchange network went completely offline due to a firewall change.
root_cause: A bad configuration change deployed to the edge firewalls blocked all HTTP and HTTPS traffic, preventing clients from connecting.
solution: Reverted the firewall configuration change and added automated validation for firewall rule sets.

issue: A commercial aircraft took off with a takeoff mass calculation that was 1,244 kg below actual weight, posing a safety risk.
root_cause: A reservation system upgrade misclassified passengers with the title 'Miss' as children, allocating them a default child weight of 35 kg instead of the adult female weight of 69 kg.
solution: Corrected the passenger title classification rules and added sanity checks comparing total checked-in counts to the load sheet.

issue: Steam gaming services suffered a widespread global outage, preventing millions of players from logging in.
root_cause: A misconfigured BGP routing announcement from an upstream transit provider (Level 3/Zayo) severed connectivity to Steam's primary data centers.
solution: Upstream providers corrected their routing filters to restore traffic flow.

issue: The entire ARPANET network crashed and was completely offline for several hours due to a routing database corruption.
root_cause: A hardware malfunction in an Interface Message Processor (IMP) corrupted memory, injecting routing messages with sequence numbers that bypassed validation. This filled up node memory buffers, causing a deadlock.
solution: Physically rebooted all network nodes to purge the corrupt routing tables.

issue: A power grid failure left 55 million people without electricity across the Northeast US and parts of Canada.
root_cause: Transmission lines hit untrimmed foliage, triggering a local failure. A software race condition and bug in the GE XA/21 alarm system prevented operators from seeing the warnings, leading to a cascading failure.
solution: Fixed the software race condition in the alarm service and implemented stricter vegetation management policies.

issue: High-end server systems crashed repeatedly and suffered silent data corruption under heavy production workloads.
root_cause: Sun Microsystems shipped several generations of server chips without Error-Correcting Code (ECC) memory support, causing cosmic rays and alpha particles to flip bits in cache memory.
solution: Recalled and replaced the processor modules with ECC-enabled units.

issue: EVE Online game update installation broke user operating systems, preventing Windows from booting.
root_cause: The game updater script contained a typo that resolved the installation path incorrectly and deleted the system's critical boot.ini file from the Windows C:\ root directory.
solution: Patched the installer to block root-level file deletions and provided instructions to restore boot.ini.

issue: GitHub services went offline for several hours due to fileservers cascading STONITH power downs.
root_cause: An aggregation-switch upgrade left a link active too long during MLAG failover, causing a traffic freeze. Pacemaker clustering software interpreted this as node failure and triggered STONITH, shutting down both nodes in active/passive pairs.
solution: Manually identified and booted the primary database nodes from local consoles, and configured Pacemaker with longer timeout limits.

issue: About 10% of background job writes failed for several hours due to a split-brain ZooKeeper and Kafka cluster.
root_cause: During ZooKeeper reprovisioning, replacement hosts were added too quickly, causing them to elect a second leader. This created two distinct clusters and split Kafka broker state.
solution: Purged the duplicate ZooKeeper cluster databases, rejoined all nodes to a single cluster, and added slow-roll provisioning rates.

issue: The application suffered a 15-second outage, dropping database transaction requests.
root_cause: A database migration run inside a transaction attempted to acquire an exclusive lock on a table while a long-running read query held a shared lock, blocking all subsequent reads and writes.
solution: Added strict lock timeouts for migrations and moved large updates to background jobs.

issue: Public DNS resolution failed intermittently and panicked for many CNAME lookups during leap second transition.
root_cause: The public DNS resolver used Go's non-monotonic time.Now(). The leap second rewound the system clock by one second, producing negative duration values which made rand.Int63n() panic.
solution: Patched the code to ensure monotonic time differences and prevented negative values from being passed to rand.

issue: Linux servers deadlocked and hung during a leap second insertion, requiring manual hard reboots.
root_cause: The leap second handler ran inside a timer interrupt holding the xtime_lock. It attempted to log the event via printk, which woke up klogd which then tried to read system time, creating a circular lock dependency.
solution: Patched the kernel leap second handler to log outside the critical timer interrupt lock path.

issue: All user browser add-ons and extensions suddenly disabled themselves, rendering major websites unusable.
root_cause: A security certificate used to sign Firefox add-ons expired, causing the browser's verification system to block all extensions.
solution: Deployed a hotfix that injected a renewed certificate into the browser's trust store.

issue: CI builds hung and failed to run for hours due to scheduler queue backlog.
root_cause: Under peak load, the primary database backed up. Subsequent manual scheduler retries flooded the queues, triggering throttling limits that made schedulers back off.
solution: Cleared backlogs by restarting build queues and added rate-limiting on manual build retries.

issue: Users experienced data drift and private repository routing errors for several minutes.
root_cause: A database master failover occurred. Because the failover node had a cold InnoDB buffer pool, load spiked and triggered a second failover back to a stale master, causing 7 minutes of data drift.
solution: Manually synced the databases and implemented warm buffer pool sharing for replica nodes.

issue: GitHub services degraded repeatedly over nine days due to database connection failures.
root_cause: A series of ProxySQL failures occurred because the OS file descriptor limit (LimitNOFILE) was capped at a low default of 65,536 due to systemd limits, despite being configured for 1 billion.
solution: Corrected systemd file descriptor configurations and restarted ProxySQL clusters.

issue: GitHub services went offline multiple times due to database connection pool saturation.
root_cause: High traffic combined with an inefficient query pattern on the shared mysql1 database cluster exhausted ProxySQL connection limits.
solution: Optimized database index queries and added proactive connection rate-limiting for backend API requests.

issue: GitHub pull requests and page updates failed to load for over 10 hours.
root_cause: A database connection rollout saturated Git database pools. The subsequent rollback triggered replica disconnects, leaving the primary node to serve all read traffic alone.
solution: Reattached database replica nodes and added backoff to database connection updates.

issue: Core GitHub services degraded globally under high load, returning 500 error pages.
root_cause: A configuration change reduced a user settings cache TTL from 12 hours to 2 hours. Under peak load, this caused a 10x spike in database write queries, overloading the cluster.
solution: Reverted the cache TTL to 12 hours and scaled cache nodes.

issue: All virtual machine provisioning operations (Actions, Codespaces) failed globally for over five hours.
root_cause: A telemetry configuration gap caused security policies to be automatically applied to backend storage accounts, which blocked critical VM metadata access in the underlying cloud provider.
solution: Reverted the auto-applied security policies and added telemetry validation checks to prevent incorrect policy enforcement.

issue: Widespread token validation failures hit Actions, Pages, and Git over HTTPS operations for nearly ten hours.
root_cause: The primary key of the scoped tokens database table reached its maximum value for a signed 32-bit integer (2,147,483,647), blocking all subsequent insertions.
solution: Ran an emergency schema migration to alter the ID column from INT to BIGINT (64-bit) and built linter checks to monitor table key usage.

issue: GitHub platform services went down due to a major power disruption at their primary data center.
root_cause: A utility power loss at the primary hosting facility was followed by a failover anomaly where backup power distribution units failed to switch load properly.
solution: Restored utility power, manually brought network and storage frames back online, and redistributed cluster instances to redundant power circuits.

issue: TravisCI builds began failing platform-wide immediately after an infrastructure deployment.
root_cause: A configuration change introduced a syntax error in the cluster scheduler configuration. A subsequent rollback attempt failed because the deployment tooling itself relied on the broken scheduler.
solution: Manually corrected the scheduler syntax on the cluster master nodes to break the circular dependency.

issue: Production database tables were accidentally truncated during a test run.
root_cause: An environment variable setting pointing to the staging database was omitted in a test script, causing the integration test harness to connect to and run truncation tasks against the production database.
solution: Restored database state from the latest point-in-time snapshot and restricted test execution environments from containing production credentials.

issue: CircleCI build workflow triggering and job scheduling suffered major delays following a database upgrade.
root_cause: A major-version blue/green database upgrade succeeded, but a secondary update immediately after rendered the database query optimizer statistics stale. Without indexes, all queries ran full table scans against disk.
solution: Re-promoted the blue (old) database to quickly restore operations, and adjusted the migration sequence to run ANALYZE immediately post-cutover.

issue: GitHub.com writes and repository updates were degraded and restricted for over 24 hours to prevent data loss.
root_cause: A brief 43-second network partition between East Coast and West Coast data centers triggered an automated MySQL primary failover. Because of replication lag, the newly promoted primary was missing recent writes, causing out-of-sync database drift.
solution: Paused user writes, ran a custom script to reconcile the database replicas manually, and restored clean replication streams.

issue: A configuration change in the Tiered Cache system caused status code 530 errors for users globally.
root_cause: A change to the Tiered Cache system had a blind spot in testing, releasing a bug that caused status code 530 failures in production, impacting about 5% of requests at peak.
solution: Rolled back the Tiered Cache configuration update and added additional test scenarios for Cache systems.

issue: Google Cloud VMware Engine (GCVE) customer clusters were automatically deleted, causing permanent data loss.
root_cause: Initial GCVE provisioning was done using a legacy option with a fixed-term contract that lacked automatic renewal, triggering automated deletion workflows at the end of the term.
solution: Restored customer workloads from external backups and updated internal provisioning accounts to prevent automatic expiration of infrastructure services.

issue: Google Compute Engine instances lost external network connectivity globally for 18 minutes.
root_cause: An autogenerated network configuration change contained a defect that removed all Google Compute Engine IP blocks from external BGP announcements.
solution: Reverted the automated network configuration change and improved safety checks in the IP block generation scripts.

issue: Elevated error rates for Google HTTP/S Load Balancers for 22 minutes.
root_cause: A software bug in the configuration deployment pipeline triggered a crash in the load balancer proxy software under specific reload conditions.
solution: Rolled back the configuration deployment and patched the load balancer proxy reload behavior.

issue: Widespread outages across Google Cloud Platform services (GCP, Gmail, YouTube) in the eastern US.
root_cause: Two distinct network misconfigurations, combined with an undetected software bug in the network control plane, isolated multiple Google data centers.
solution: Manually re-routed backbone traffic and applied a hotfix to the network control plane software.

issue: Power loss in a data center caused degraded performance and instance termination for EC2.
root_cause: A physical transformer failed, and a Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) managing generator synchronization crashed, preventing backup generators from powering up.
solution: Replaced the failed PLC and established manual override protocols for datacenter power synchronization.

issue: Power outages throughout AWS US East Region led to degradation of EC2 instances and EBS volumes.
root_cause: Severe storms disrupted utility power, and a backup generator failed to provide stable voltage, causing failover mechanisms to drop load.
solution: Upgraded backup generator monitoring and modified voltage regulator failover margins.

issue: A power outage at an AWS Sydney facility caused failures across multiple Availability Zones.
root_cause: Severe local weather disrupted the main electrical grid, and a breaker failure on the backup generation circuit cut power to cooling systems.
solution: Manually bypassed the failed breaker, restored power to cooling loops, and improved breaker redundancy.

issue: Utility power loss at a São Paulo AZ disrupted EBS and EC2 instances.
root_cause: Grid power failed, and one backup generator's output breaker opened due to current spike, while a second generator failed mechanically.
solution: Repaired the generator mechanical failure and adjusted breaker trip thresholds for backup generation lines.

issue: An entire AWS data center lost cooling capability, forcing emergency hardware shutdowns.
root_cause: A software bug in the third-party PLC control system code caused excessive communications loops during a control-host failover, crashing the cooling control logic.
solution: Patched the PLC software to rate-limit inter-controller state communications.

issue: A DynamoDB outage in US-East-1 cascaded into a region-wide cloud service disruption.
root_cause: A latent race condition in DynamoDB's automated DNS management left the regional endpoint with an empty DNS record, blocking client requests.
solution: Manually restored DNS records and disabled the automated DNS updater script pending a fix.

issue: Slow network configuration changes frozen on Google Cloud load balancers for ~2 hours.
root_cause: A series of complex configuration updates triggered a very slow path in the load balancer management logic, causing configuration processing queues to block.
solution: Restarted the management worker services and refactored the configuration processing serialization.

issue: Increased network latency and packet loss across Google Cloud Services in central US.
root_cause: A hardware component on a primary fiber backbone path failed, and failover traffic saturated secondary network paths.
solution: Replaced the failed fiber path component and adjusted capacity allocation across redundant routes.

issue: Customer incident IDs jumped by exactly 32 (e.g. from INC-7 to INC-39).
root_cause: A Postgres database High Availability (HA) upgrade promoted a new replica, causing database sequence caches to skip IDs by their pre-allocated cache size of 32.
solution: Adjusted the sequence cache sizes to prevent large ID gaps during planned replica failovers.

issue: The WebKit repository became corrupted and unavailable for commits.
root_cause: Two PDF files with identical SHA-1 hash values (SHA-1 collision) were checked in, breaking the Subversion repository's storage deduplication mechanism.
solution: Removed the duplicate-hash files, updated the SVN server to reject files matching known collision signatures, and migrated toward SHA-256.

issue: GitHub write operations degraded, and repository updates delayed for several hours.
root_cause: A network partition between data centers triggered automated primary promotion, but the chosen replica had stale replication streams.
solution: Manually forced failover to the correct database node and restarted write operations.

issue: GitHub Actions workflow queues delayed and runner communication failing.
root_cause: Redis connection limits on the orchestrator were exceeded due to a connection leak introduced in a worker service deployment.
solution: Rolled back the worker deployment, terminated leaky connections, and raised limits.

issue: Jira and Confluence Cloud sites deleted for 775 customer accounts, lasting 14 days.
root_cause: An automated script designed to purge legacy plugin data ran with incorrect parameters, deleting customer sites and their backup metadata.
solution: Restored customer databases manually from physical snapshots and added multi-engineer approvals for destructive script execution.

issue: ChatGPT offline; users exposed to other active users' chat titles and payment details.
root_cause: A bug in the redis-py Redis client library caused connections to be recycled with incorrect session context under heavy load.
solution: Patched the redis-py library to clear connection state upon context validation failure.

issue: ChatGPT API and web interface experiencing high error rates and timeouts.
root_cause: A distributed denial of service (DDoS) attack saturated the edge proxies and gateway controllers.
solution: Implemented stricter WAF rate-limiting rules and isolated traffic from known malicious IP blocks.

issue: Amazon Kinesis outage degraded Cognito, IAM, and ECS services in US-East-1.
root_cause: A network scale-up exceeded connection limits in the internal Kinesis routing service, triggering a control plane failure loop.
solution: Rolled back the network scale-up, restarted routers, and isolated control plane traffic paths.

issue: Elevated error rates and timeout latencies for AWS Lambda invocations in US-East-1.
root_cause: A configuration deployment to Lambda routing proxies caused CPU starvation under peak load.
solution: Rolled back the proxy configuration changes and scaled routing nodes to handle load.

issue: Widespread global CDN outage, taking down Reddit, Twitch, GitHub, and major news sites.
root_cause: A specific customer configuration update triggered a latent software bug in the edge cache parser, crashing the service.
solution: Disabled the specific configuration setting pattern and deployed a software hotfix to the edge nodes.

issue: Global Edge DNS resolution failed, making customer domains unreachable.
root_cause: A routing table configuration update triggered a bug in the Akamai Edge DNS resolver daemon, causing processes to crash.
solution: Reverted the routing table update and restarted the DNS resolver daemon.

issue: Webhook delivery delays and failures for several hours.
root_cause: A message queue (Kafka) broker disk partition reached 100% capacity due to logging rotation failure, blocking message commits.
solution: Purged outdated log partitions, increased disk limits, and enabled automatic log recycling.

issue: Heroku Connect sync between Salesforce and Postgres failing.
root_cause: An API update in Salesforce modified field serialization order, breaking the parsing logic in Heroku Connect.
solution: Released a client parser hotfix that supports dynamic field indexing, and restarted sync workers.

issue: CircleCI security alert: compromised secrets, keys, and environment variables.
root_cause: Malware on an engineer's laptop bypassed MFA, allowing session token theft and subsequent access to backend backup stores.
solution: Revoked all user API tokens, rotated internal secrets, and updated endpoint detection software.

issue: GitHub API returning HTTP 503 errors and blocking Git operations.
root_cause: A faulty routing policy deployed to the API gateway caused request routing redirect loops.
solution: Reverted the API gateway routing configuration and restarted edge proxies.

issue: ChatGPT users exposed to other active chat session data.
root_cause: A race condition in session mapping logic during high traffic volume peaks mixed up user context keys.
solution: Implemented strict session-isolation scopes and refactored thread locks on connection managers.

issue: Git clones and pushes failing intermittently due to file server errors.
root_cause: A file storage array array controller hardware failure led to data corruption on primary volumes.
solution: Activated secondary controller paths and synchronized volumes from replica logs.

issue: Discord clients stuck on connecting; users unable to load chat channels.
root_cause: A database node failure in the ScyllaDB cluster triggered request timeouts that cascaded into gateway hub thread starvation.
solution: Scaled the database nodes, applied client rate limiting, and restarted edge hubs.

issue: 1.1.1.1 public DNS resolver returning SERVFAIL responses.
root_cause: DNSSEC validation failed in resolver software after a key rotation mismatch caused invalid signatures.
solution: Temporarily disabled DNSSEC checks, synced keys, and re-enabled validation.

issue: GitHub Gists and Pages unavailable, returning database errors.
root_cause: An unoptimized search query triggered database write locks, exhausting active connection pools.
solution: Optimized the query, terminated locking transactions, and added database rate limits.

issue: Webhook delivery delays of up to several hours.
root_cause: A queue queue capacity limit bug in the webhook broker caused delivery worker starvation.
solution: Pushed a hotfix to expand queue capacities and scaled consumer nodes.

issue: SMS and push notifications delayed for several minutes.
root_cause: A downstream SMS aggregator network connection degraded, backing up notification dispatcher buffers.
solution: Switched traffic to backup SMS providers and increased dispatcher queue capacities.

issue: Heroku revoked all customer GitHub integration tokens.
root_cause: A database security breach exposed customer OAuth tokens to an unauthorized third party.
solution: Revoked all integration tokens, rotated GitHub OAuth credentials, and prompted manual reconnections.

issue: GitHub Package Registry publishing operations delayed or returning HTTP 500 errors.
root_cause: An unindexed metadata lookup query in the registry backend database triggered 100% CPU lock on active read replicas.
solution: Pushed an indexing migration script to the database and scaled up registry replica pools.

issue: Codespaces creation and session loading experiencing elevated latency.
root_cause: Hypervisor host connection limit reached in the primary region due to slow container cleanup routines.
solution: Manually purged idle hypervisor containers and optimized cleanup daemon check frequencies.

issue: GitHub Copilot completions experiencing timeouts and failed requests.
root_cause: A configuration drift in the model gateway proxies restricted keep-alive socket reuse, flooding backend clusters.
solution: Corrected the proxy configuration setting and re-aligned keep-alive parameters across regions.

issue: SSH and HTTPS Git authentication failing intermittently for over an hour.
root_cause: A memory allocation failure in the internal user-session cache cluster led to authentication lookups falling back to slow DB paths.
solution: Restarted the affected cache nodes and increased cache cluster RAM allocation limits.

issue: Pull Requests pages loading slowly or failing to render diffs.
root_cause: A high volume of concurrent commits to monorepos triggered lock queues on git file servers.
solution: Adjusted PR diff-rendering concurrency limits and enabled aggressive diff caching rules.

issue: GitHub Pages deployment pipelines stuck in queued state.
root_cause: A certificate renewal task hung in a locked state, blocking subsequent deployment queue consumers.
solution: Killed the blocked renewal task, restarted deployment worker services, and added execution timeouts.

issue: Webhook notifications and integrations processing delayed by up to 30 minutes.
root_cause: A database schema change in the integration metadata table locked query execution paths in the delivery worker broker.
solution: Rolled back the schema change and rescheduled the update for off-peak hours.

issue: GitHub Actions orchestrator experiencing slow run initiations.
root_cause: A memory leak in the runner orchestration Go service led to slow garbage collection sweeps, increasing scheduling times.
solution: Rolled back the orchestrator service release to a stable version and debugged the leak.

issue: Issues, Projects, and Milestones creation failing with internal database write locks.
root_cause: A routine database index optimization job on the main tickets table acquired exclusive tables locks under active load.
solution: Terminated the optimization job, optimized locking queries, and deferred indexes build.

issue: GitHub API Gateway returning high TLS handshake timeouts for developer queries.
root_cause: A configuration drift in API gateway SSL cipher settings caused CPU exhaustion on load balancers during peak traffic.
solution: Reverted the SSL cipher configuration changes to the standard set.

issue: Repository archiving and download requests failing with HTTP 504 gateway timeouts.
root_cause: Storage mount disk latency spiked in the archive storage array because of a disk controller card failure.
solution: Replaced the failed storage array controller card and synchronized data streams.

issue: Gist read/write operations experiencing intermittent failures.
root_cause: Redis session cluster for Gists became saturated due to a connection leak in Gist client components.
solution: Patched the Gist client wrapper to correctly release connections and restarted the session cluster.

issue: ChatGPT Plugin Directory unavailable or returning connection errors.
root_cause: A bug in the plugin directory search service triggered query parsing infinite loops under specific text symbols.
solution: Patched the directory search query parser code and restarted search API nodes.

issue: OpenAI Fine-Tuning API jobs failing to start or stuck in execution.
root_cause: A thread pool exhaustion in the fine-tuning orchestrator blocked job schedule queues.
solution: Increased fine-tuning orchestrator thread pool sizes and scaled computing nodes.

issue: OpenAI Moderation endpoint requests experiencing high latency and HTTP 504 timeouts.
root_cause: A database scale-up in the moderation policy registry caused write deadlocks on the moderation servers.
solution: Aborted the policy scale-up and optimized database lock parameters in the moderation service.

issue: Multiple SimpleDB storage nodes lost power simultaneously in one US-East data center.
root_cause: The lock service de-registered them rapidly, which spiked load and pushed handshake latencies above SimpleDB's too-aggressive handshake timeout. Healthy storage and metadata nodes failed their handshakes, removed themselves from the cluster, and couldn't rejoin because the metadata nodes that would authorize them had also taken themselves out.
solution: Recovery required manually raising the handshake timeout and restarting metadata nodes.

issue: A GitHub personal access token with recently elevated scopes was leaked from Homebrew’s Jenkins that allowed access to `git push` on several Homebrew repositories.
root_cause: Consequently, no packages were compromised, and no action is required by users due to this incident. While the project already had 2FA and third-party application restrictions enabled for its GitHub organization, a recommendation to use GPG signing for `Homebrew/homebrew-core` was considered but ultimately rejected due to workflow concerns.
solution: Within a few hours of the report, the compromised credentials were revoked, replaced, and sanitized within Jenkins to prevent future exposure. Consequently, no packages were compromised, and no action is required by users due to this incident.

issue: Another story of multiple incidents that ended up impacting [query performance](https://status.honeycomb.io/incidents/fzw6hqjx5t4f) and [alerting via triggers and SLOs](https://status.honeycomb.io/incidents/jwhrxcs5zr06).
root_cause: In early August 2022, Honeycomb experienced incidents impacting query performance and alerting via triggers and SLOs. Visible issues began around 11:35 a.m. ET, with the worst impact lasting approximately 4 hours, though the investigation spanned 9 hours. The incidents stemmed from a convergence of factors.
solution: These incidents were notable because of how challenging their investigation turned out to be.

issue: A bad event (poison pill) in the async workers queue triggered unhandled panics that repeatedly crashed the app.
root_cause: This combined poorly with Heroku infrastructure, making it difficult to find the source of the problem.
solution: Applied mitigations that are generally interesting to people running web services, such as catching corner cases of Go panic recovery and splitting work by type/class to improve reliability.

issue: After the primary locked up and was restarted, it was brought back up with the wrong filesystem, causing a global outage.
root_cause: See also [HN discussion](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=8003601).
solution: See also [HN discussion](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=8003601).

issue: The Order Management System (OMS) provided to Zerodha, a stock broker, collapsed when an order for 1M units of a penny stock was divided into more than 0.1M individual trades against the typical few hundreds, triggering a collapse of the OMS, which was not encountered prior by its provider - Refinitiv (formerly Thomson Reuters), a subsidiary of the London Stock Exchange.
root_cause: The root cause was identified as an unprecedented event: a single order for 10 lakh units of a sub-Rs 1 stock, placed around 9:40 AM on BSE, was executed in over 1 lakh individual trades. This highly unusual fragmentation of a single order, far exceeding the typical few hundred trades, caused an overload in the OMS, a scenario neither Zerodha nor its vendor, Refinitiv (formerly Thomson Reuters), had encountered before.
solution: Refinitiv is actively working on a fix for the OMS to better handle such extreme cases of order execution.

issue: A failure of the primary leased line to a CTCL between a stock broker and a stock exchange led to the activation of a backup leased line that was operating sporadically over the following hour, affecting bracket and cover orders.
